## The Realignment Architecture

A provenance-first, human-governed research architecture for systems that must earn trust.

R1 moves beyond a prospectus-only release: it publishes bounded implementation evidence, preserved semantic-test failures, a source-frozen reproduction of the Ubay rainfall–ENSO association, explicit correction history, and a reuse-first engineering strategy.

[Read the flagship R1 →](articles/realignment-architecture-prospectus.qmd)
[Inspect the RQ5 evidence note →](articles/rq5-ubay-enso-reproduction.qmd)
:::

::: {.release-abstract}
**Evidence boundary**<br>
The reproduced RQ5 relationship is an association, not a causal mechanism. The latest semantic correction is regression evidence on a seen suite, not new generalization evidence.

**Release posture**<br>
Failures, abstentions, disagreements, missing evidence, and negative controls remain part of the public record.
:::
:::

## Publication standard

::: {.publication-standard}
::: {}
### Inspectable

Material claims identify their evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, and break conditions.
:::

::: {}
### Revisioned

Every public release states its status and revision; corrections replace the controlling version without erasing provenance.
:::

::: {}
### Human-gated

AI may assist research and drafting, but consequential decisions remain attributable to accountable people.
:::
:::

Each release is labeled by status and revision. The purpose is to make claims inspectable, preserve credible disagreement, and expose ideas to correction—not to present unfinished concepts as established science or deployable products.
